title: K-Pop Met Punjabi Pop and the Internet Lost Its Mind. BOOMPALA Just Changed the Rules.
excerpt: LE SSERAFIM's chart-busting single gets a desi remix from Guru Randhawa — the first K-pop and Indian artist collab of its kind, four languages deep, and a statement about where global pop is heading.
body:
There is a moment in the new visualizer for BOOMPALA (feat. Guru Randhawa) where the Punjabi verses slide in over a Latin-house beat built on a Macarena sample, and you realize three continents of pop music are happening simultaneously. Korean, English, Spanish, Punjabi — all in one track, none of it forced, all of it absurdly danceable. This is either the future of global pop or the most fun anybody's had with a remix in years. Possibly both.

https://youtube.com/watch?v=0CEg8nz_I9U

Released on June 6, the official remix pairs LE SSERAFIM — the five-member HYBE-backed K-pop powerhouse — with Guru Randhawa, India's most-streamed Punjabi pop export, in what is the first collaboration between a K-pop group and an Indian artist of this scale. LE SSERAFIM dropped the announcement on Instagram to over 112,000 likes within hours. The track is out on all major platforms via Source Music and Warner Music India.

A Viral Hit Gets a Punjabi Makeover

The original BOOMPALA arrived on May 22 as the lead single of LE SSERAFIM's second studio album PUREFLOW Pt. 1, which debuted at No. 10 on the Billboard 200 and topped Billboard's Top Album Sales chart. The track racked up over 18 million Spotify streams and 10 million YouTube views in its first four days alone. It entered the U.S. Billboard Bubbling Under Hot 100 at No. 10.

Indian fans had already spotted the connections. The original music video featured yoga-inspired choreography and the word namaste woven into the visuals — small desi touches that felt deliberate. The Guru Randhawa remix makes that subtext text.

"LE SSERAFIM is incredible and BOOMPALA already has an infectious energy that reminds me of the massive, celebratory vibe we love in India. Bringing a touch of my signature style to a Latin-house K-pop track sampling Macarena felt like a beautiful masterpiece." — Guru Randhawa

Randhawa — known for billion-stream anthems like Lahore, High Rated Gabru, and Suit Suit — has built an international profile through collaborations with Pitbull, Jay Sean, The Chainsmokers, Rick Ross, and French Montana. But a K-pop collaboration is new territory entirely, and it positions him at the intersection of two of the world's fastest-growing music markets.

Why This Matters for the Diaspora

For millions of Indian listeners abroad — especially younger fans who toggle between K-pop playlists and Bollywood party tracks — BOOMPALA is the crossover they didn't know they were waiting for. The remix doesn't ask you to choose between cultures. It stacks them.

LE SSERAFIM — Kim Chaewon, Sakura, Huh Yunjin, Kazuha, and Hong Eunchae — have been strategic about expanding beyond East and Southeast Asian markets. This collaboration signals India and the South Asian diaspora as a serious frontier.

"When we created BOOMPALA, our goal was to bring people together across different generations and cultures through a shared, festival-like energy. Guru's incredible Indian artistry brought an entirely new, vibrant life to the track." — LE SSERAFIM

The lyrics now flow seamlessly across four languages without a single jarring transition. Randhawa's Punjabi verses arrive with the swagger of a festival headliner walking into someone else's set and owning it. The Latin-house production holds everything together like the world's best DJ reading a room of 8 billion people.

The Bigger Picture

This isn't just a nice remix. It's a data point in a trend that's been building for years: the collapse of genre and geography in global pop. BTS opened the door. BLACKPINK kicked it wider. Diljit Dosanjh proved Punjabi music could fill arenas from Vancouver to Birmingham. Now LE SSERAFIM and Guru Randhawa are proving that a Korean girl group and a Punjabi hitmaker can share the same four minutes and have it sound completely natural.

The BOOMPALA visualizer is streaming now on YouTube and all major platforms. The album PUREFLOW Pt. 1 is available on Spotify, Apple Music, and Amazon Music.

If the vibes of this remix are anything to go by, the question isn't whether K-pop and desi pop will collaborate again. It's how quickly everyone else catches up.
